en: 1. Oṃ, homage to the illustrious Mahābhairava! Homage to the illustrious Kubjikā!
Worship of the deities of the Guru-maṇḍala; the water offering (argha) for the Sun; the flower vessel; the extraction of the maṇḍala (cakra-uddhāra).
One should worship Navātman, situated in the center of the Guru-maṇḍala, within a diagram consisting of a central triangle, an eight-petaled lotus, and a square provided with gates.
The extraction of the Navātma-cakra; the worship of the deities of the Guru-maṇḍala.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ, I worship the sandals of the venerable Guru.
hsauṃ hsphrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ||
Aiṁ (5). Salutation to that venerable Guru by whom that state was revealed—the undivided, eternal sphere which pervades all that is moving and unmoving.
Aiṃ (5). To the lotus seat, svāhā. (3). Sandals to the leaf seat. Sandals to the tortoise seat.
Āsana: Aiṃ (5) Kini Vicce Koṅkanāya Hra Astrāya Phaṭ. (3) ||
lāhile || aiṁ (5) aiṁ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā || (3) ||
Aiṃ (5) Aiṃ, O Kula-mountain, you who are moving in the non-Kula! Hrāṃ hrīṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Aiṃ (5) Aiṃ kiṇi kiṇi vicce koṅkanāya hraṃḥ astrāya phaṭ.
Purification of the hands.
Aiṃ (5) | Homage to the Blessed Lady Hṛtkamalā; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ to Aṅguṣṭhā (3).
Aiṃ (5) to Kubjikā, the Island of the Kula; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ to the Tarjanī [finger] (3).
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Varvalaśikhe Hrūṃ, salutation to the Middle One (3).
Aiṃ (5) Ghore Aghore Aghorāmukhī Bahurūpāyai Hre Śrī-Anāmikāyai (3).
Aiṃ (5) Chāṃ Chīṃ, salutation to Mahantārikā; Hrauṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to Kaniṣṭhā. (3)
Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi kiṇi Vicce Koṅkanāya Hraṃḥ Śrīkaratarāya (3).
Karanyāsa (the ritual placement on the hands)
Aiṁ (5) Homage to the Blessed One, to the Lotus of the Heart; Hrīṁ Śrīṁ, to the upward-facing one, the sandals.
Aiṃ (5) Hsphreṃ! To Kubjikā, the island of the Kula, to the eastern face. (3)
Aiṁ (5) Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hrūṁ, O you with the curly locks! Hruṁ, to the glorious Southern Face (3).
Aiṃ (5) Ghore Aghore Aghorāmukhī Bahurūpāya Śrī-Uttaravaktrāya (3).
Aiṃ (5) Chāṃ Chīṃ, to Mahantakāya, to the venerable Western Face (3).
Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi kiṇi Vicce! To Koṅkanā, the mouth of Śrī Parā (3).
Thus ends the placement upon the face.
Aiṃ (5) Homage to the Blessed One, to the Lotus of the Heart; Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, homage to the heart.
Aiṃ (5) Hsphreṃ, svāhā to Kubjikā, the island of the Kula, Hrīṃ Śrī, to the stone seat!
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Varvalaśikhe Hrūṃ; [this is] for the tuft of hair, Vauṣaṭ.
Aiṃ (5) Ghore, Aghore, Aghorāmukhī, Bahurūpāya, to the glorious Kavaca, Hūṃ!
Aiṃ (5) Chāṃ Chīṃ, to Mahantārikā, Hrauṃ, to the three eyes of Śrī, Vauṣaṭ!
Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi kiṇi Vicce Koṅkanāyai Hraḥ Astrāya Phaṭ!
Thus ends the ritual placement of the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*).
Then follows the worship of the water vessel.
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ! To Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda, the Lord of Heroes, Śkṣmlvryīṃ!
[I offer] the venerable water-vessel and the sandals. Hrāṃ! [Perform] the invocation and so forth for the heart and other limbs. One should display the cow-mudrā.
Gāyatrī: We know Kubjikā; we meditate upon Kuladvīpa;
may that Kubjī inspire us. [This is] the sprinkling of all substances, beginning with the self.
Then follows the worship with the vessel of honor (arghapātra).
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Hreṃḥ Praphura (2) Ghora (2) Tanu Tanu Rūpacaṭa (2) Kaha (2) Vama (2) Dama (2) Ghātaya (2) Vighātaya (2) Vighni (2) Hūṃ (3) Phaṭ Kroṃ Śrī-Mahākaumārikā Vicce Pādukāṃ.
ŚKṢMLVYĪṂ! To Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda Virādhipati, Śrī Mahāvidyārājeśvarī HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ! [I offer] the sandals for the venerable argha-vessel.
Hrāṃ for the heart and other limbs; perform the rites beginning with invocation (āvāhana); show the yoni-mudrā.
Then follows the kacchapamudrā.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hsphreṃ Hsphroṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ. By this, the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi) is performed.

Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ. To Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda, the Lord of Heroes, Śkṣmlvryīṃ. For myself, for the cutting away of sins: flowers, sandals, unguent, sandalwood, sandals, Hrīṃ—the reality, the eye-salve, sandals, the sacred ash of the Hero, vermilion (3).
Hsphrāṃ, the enchantress of all people (3). Hsauṃ, various parasols, ornaments, and flowers (3).
Having tied the *kusā* grass, one should sprinkle water from the three vessels onto the ring finger.
Then, having offered the five-fold oblation (pañcabali), one should recite the Mālinī invocation.
Aiṃ (5) to the one seated upon a peacock throne (3). Aiṃ (5) Śrīṃ Hrīṃ to Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha (3).

Aiṃ! O Devīputra Vaṭukanātha, radiant with the mass of your monkey-like matted locks, three-eyed, flame-mouthed one, descend! Come, come, O Blessed One, into the center of the maṇḍala; accept the offering as it has been presented, and may you rejoice in the desired object! Some hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
Aiṃ (5) Narāsanāya (3) || Kṣāṃ Kṣūṃ Kṣetrapālāya (3) ||
Aiṃ! (5) Come, come, O Lord of the Vast Abode, by the name of Jatha; descend (2), descend into the center of the maṇḍala (2)!
You who possess four arms, three eyes, and so forth, hold the khaṭvāṅga, sword, shield, and trident in your hands!
O you who wear great skull ornaments, whose radiance is equal to ten million flashes of lightning, come, come, O Blessed One, in your terrifying form;
accept [this offering] as it has been presented for the sake of shrouding my obstacles! Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ phaṭ svāhā!
To the lion-throne (3). To those who belong to the Yoginīs (3).

Aiṃ (5). Whatever [mantras] belong to the yogis, born of all the pīṭhas, born of the fields, born of yoga, born of the womb, born of the kṣelas, born of the sandohas, or born of the prasandohas; whatever [mantras] belong to the yogis—whether they be *khecarīs*, *bhūcarīs*, *gocarīs*, or those consisting of one syllable, two syllables, three syllables, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, or ten syllables, or those possessing the three junctions (*trijujña*).
O you who have arrived according to [your vows], accept this offering; grant me success! HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ PHAṬ SVĀHĀ.
Aiṃ (5) pādukāṃ for the seat of the pretas. Aiṃ (5) hkhphreṃ, O Śrī Siddhicāmuṇḍeśvarī, accept the bali (2) svāhā. 4. Aiṃ (5) pādukāṃ for the seat of the mouse.
Aiṃ (5) Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaḥ, accept the sandals and the offering for the venerable Kulagaṇeśvara;
Svāhā! (5) Then, having shaken [the vessel], offer the great offering (māhābali) with Svāhā.
All [of them] have tawny hair and four tawny eyes; they are said to be the witnesses. Jvālā: Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ!
Accept the bali offering from the Kṣetrapālas of your own respective abodes! Svāhā! (2)
Aiṃ! O you of great power, radiant with the mass of tawny matted locks, three-eyed one with flaming mouths, accept the offering of bees, the sacrificial cake, and the flesh!
In the form of Bhairava, *turu* (twice), *muru* (twice), *khakha* (twice), *lala* (twice)! O Lord of the Great Ḍāmaras, svāhā!
With that mantra, one should offer the bali-oblation in one's own field.

Perform the invocation and other rites with sandalwood paste, unbroken rice grains, and flowers, saying "Namaḥ. One should display the staff, the threatening finger, the dot, the womb, and the elephant mudrās. [Offer] incense, lamps, and food offerings.

Japa: (*? Svāhā (10), Kṣāṃ Svāhā (10), Jāṃ Svāhā (10), Hskhphreṃ Svāhā (10), Glau Svāhā (10). Stotra: Aiṃ (5) [I praise] the son of Gaurī, Kumāra, whose body is like the sky, the guardian of the field (kṣetrapa), and the Yoginīs.
One should worship with devotion Cāmuṇḍā of fierce form, Gaṇeśa whose face is that of the lord of elephants and who destroys obstacles,

and the Lord of the Circle (Cakreśa) with flowers, incense, lamps, meat, honey, and offerings; may He destroy the misfortunes of those who are worshipped and grant both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
In this ritual for the five world-protectors, may all that be perfectly complete.
Then follows the purification of the principles (tattva-śodhana): the consumption of betel leaves and so forth, as well as wine and meat.
Again, Aiṃ (5): the invocation of Śrī Saṃvartānā.
Aiṃ (5) Aṃ, the sandals of the primordial god Śrī-Ādideva of the infinite maṇḍala; with that, [offer] the bali.
Then follows the worship of the three deities.
The sandals for the one seated on a man; the sandals for the one seated on a peacock; the sandals for the one seated on a rat.
Meditative concentration.
Aiṃ. (5) The god is seated upon a corpse-throne, blue in color and with a single face;
he has three eyes and six arms, and the god holds a sword and a shield, while his hands also carry a hand-drum, a khaṭvāṅga, a dot, and a skull-cup.
One should meditate upon Kṣetrapālaka, whose limbs are adorned with a shaven head, bones, and other ornaments.
Homage to the flower of meditative concentration.
KṢĀṂ KṢĪṂ KṢŪṂ KṢAIṂ KṢAUṂ KṢAḤ, the sandals for the venerable Kṣetrapāla.
Accept this offering, svāhā!
The sandals for the peacock posture.
Meditative concentration.
Mounted upon a great peacock, she has the form of a youth;
her body is adorned with red skulls, and she holds a staff, a spear, and a boon-granting gesture.
The glorious Bindumudrā-kara, adorned with red power—
thus I meditate upon and bow to the god Vaṭukanātha.
Homage to the flower of meditative concentration.
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Hrīṃ, the sandals for the noble son Vaṭukanātha; the offering.
The sandals for Mūśāsana. Meditation.
Aiṁ (5): Seated upon the back of a rat, with handsome limbs and an elephant's face, possessing three eyes, he holds an axe, a *laḍūka* fruit, and a rosary of rudrākṣa beads.
Having thus meditated upon Gaṇanātha, the great boon-granter, whose body has a serpent for a sacred thread, who destroys all misfortune, and who removes all obstacles;
Homage to the flower of meditative concentration.
Gāṃ gīṃ gūṃ gaiṃ gauṃ gaḥ glauṃ. To the venerable Lord of the Kula-gaṇas, the sandals. Offering.
The rites beginning with the invocation (āvāhana).
Then, the worship of the directions (digpūjā).
Homage to the one seated upon a swan. Homage to the one seated upon an elephant.

Aiṃ (5). To the Great Bhairava Aśitāṅga at the great sacred site of Prayāga, together with the Śakti Brahmāṇī, to the Kṣetrapāla Hetuka, the Lord of the Gods, obeisance! These [mantras] are for the East.
To the seat of the Fire-god, obeisance! To the seat of the bull, obeisance! To the seat of the goat, obeisance!
Aiṃ (5). Homage to the Great Kṣetrapāla Ruru Mahābhairava, together with the Śakti Māheśvarī, the Lord of the Field Tripurāntaka, and the Sovereign of Splendor.
To the one on the southern side: homage to the one seated upon a peacock, to the one seated upon a buffalo.
Aiṁ (5). Homage to Caṇḍamahābhairava of the great sacred field of Oṃkārāpura, together with his consort Kaumārī Śakti, and to the Kṣetrapāla Agnivetāla.
To the one in the southwest: obeisance to the one seated upon Garuḍa; obeisance to the one seated upon a man.
Aiṃ (5). Homage to Aṭṭahāsa Mahākṣetra, the Great Wrathful One, the Great Terrifier, together with the Vaiṣṇavī Śakti, to Agnijihva Kṣetrapāla, the Lord of Rākṣasas; Ṭaṃ.
In the west: homage to the one seated upon a buffalo; homage to the one seated upon a crocodile.
Aiṁ (5) Oṃ. Victorious in the Great Field! Homage to Unmattamahābhairava, together with his Śakti Vārāhī, to Kālākṣa Kṣetrapāla, the Lord of Waters. Taṃ. Namaḥ.
To the northwest: obeisance to her who has an elephant as her seat; obeisance to her who has a deer as her seat.
Aiṁ (5) Oṃ, salutation to Caritalakṣetra Mahābhairava, together with the power Indrāṇī, to Kalālakṣa Kṣetrapāla, the lord of the wind.
To the northern [direction]: obeisance to Pretāsana; obeisance to Hayāsana.
Aiṁ (5) Oṃ! Homage to the Great Field of Ekāmraka, to the Terrifying Mahābhairava, together with his power Cāmuṇḍā, to the one-legged Kṣetrapāla, the Lord of Wealth.
To Īśāna, obeisance to the lion-throne; obeisance to the bull-throne.
Aiṃ (5) Oṃ! Salutation to the Great Bhairava of Destruction, the Lord of Beings, accompanied by the Śakti Mahālakṣmī, [residing] in the great sacred field of Devīkoṭa; Śaṃ.

Salutations to Garuḍāsana. Oṃ, salutations to the great Kṣetrapāla on the back of the Tortoise, the lord of the lower regions, accompanied by the power Jvālinī, together with Dāmala and the other Bhairavas, and the lord of the Nāgas.

To the one above: salutation to the Swan-throned One (Haṃsāsana). Oṃ! To Dāmāra, the Great Field (Mahākṣetra), the Sovereign of the Upper Region, accompanied by the flaming Śakti, to the Bhairava who presides over the Ḍāmalas, the Sovereign of Heaven—salutation!
Then follows the worship of the pitcher (*kalaśa*). The ritual placement (*nyāsa*): *oṃ juṃ saḥ astrāya phaṭ* (four times).
Oṃ juṃ sa aṃguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | Oṃ juṃ saḥ tarjjanībhyāṃ namaḥ |
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, salutation to the two middle fingers. Oṃ juṃ saḥ, salutation to the two ring fingers.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, salutation to the two little fingers (kaniṣṭhā). Oṃ juṃ saḥ, salutation to the backs of both hands (karatarapṛṣṭha).
Thus is the placement of the hand (iti-kara-nyāsa).
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, homage to the heart. Oṃ juṃ saḥ, svāhā to the stone.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock (śikhā). Oṃ juṃ saḥ, hūṃ to the armor (kavaca).
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes. Oṃ juṃ saḥ, phaṭ to the weapon.
The assignment of limbs is the ritual placement (nyāsa).
Aiṃ, the pādukā for the Ādhāra-seat; the pādukā for the Ananta-seat.
The sandals for the seat of Skanda; the sandals for the seat of Nara.
The sandals for the Lotus Seat; the sandals for the Filament Seat.
The sandals for the one seated upon the pericarp.
The sandals for the lotus posture.
Meditative absorption (dhyāna).
Pure, resembling a crystal, three-eyed, with the moon upon his crest, holding the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and bearing a rosary, a seal, and a plough.
Having meditated thus upon Mahādeva, one's desired object shall be accomplished.
The flower of meditative concentration is the sandal.
Mantra.
Aiṃ (5) Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghore Hrīṃ, Ghoraghoratare Huṃ Phreṃ, Sarvataḥ Sarva Sarve Hreṃ Juṃ Saḥ Hrauṃ, O you whose form is Rudra, Hrāḥ! [I worship] the sandals. (5)

Aiṁ (5) to Vajrakubjikā, Hsphrīṁ O you who subjugate the three worlds! Hrīṁ O you who melt the limbs of Kāma! Klīṁ Strīṁ O you who cause great agitation! Aiṁ Sauṁ Saḥ, [I worship] the venerable sandals.

Aiṃ (5). Homage to the Blessed One, Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā! Śrāṃ śrīṃ śrūṃ, O Khaga! Aiṃ, O Terrible One! O Non-terrible One! O You Whose Face is Not Terrible! Chāṃ chīṃ kiṇi (2), O Vircce! [I worship] the sandals.
Aiṁ (5). Homage to the Blessed One, the Siddha! Hsphrāṁ hsphrīṁ! O you whose face is not terrible, ṅa anaṇame! Chāṁ chīṁ kiṇi (2)! Vicce! [I worship] the sandal.
Aiṃ (5) Homage to the Blessed One, Hsphreṃ Kubjikā! Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ! O Terrible One, O Non-terrible One, O You Whose Face is Non-terrible!
Chāṃ Chīṃ! Kiṇi (2)! To Vircce, [I offer] the sandals.
To Brahmā, a pair of sandals. To Viṣṇu. To Rudra. To Īśvara. To Sadāśiva.
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, to the Great Bhairava Amṛtīśa, the Conqueror of Death (Mṛtyuñjaya), accompanied by the power (śakti) Amṛtamahālakṣmī;
Oṃ juṃ saḥ, [I offer] the sandals. At the end of the fortnight (2).
Salutations to Mārgaśīrṣa and the other twelve months. Salutations to the seasons. Salutations to the year. (Twice each).
Salutation to the seven oceans beginning with the Bitter (Kṣāra). Salutation to the ten world-protectors beginning with Indra.
To the nine planets beginning with Āditya; (2) salutation to the twenty-eight lunar mansions beginning with Aśvinī.
Salutations to the twenty-seven yogas beginning with Viṣkambha. Salutations to the sixteen lunar days (tithis) beginning with Pratipadā.
Salutation to the twelve zodiac signs beginning with Aries, and to the sixteen daily muhūrtas beginning with Rudra.
Salutation to the sixteen muhūrtas beginning with Girīśa. Salutation to the seven rivers beginning with Gaṅgā.
Salutation to Aśvasthāman and the others, the eight long-lived ones. Salutation to Śātī.
Homage to Vidyā, Kalā, Nivṛtti, and Pratiṣṭhā.

Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ. To the great army of the Kula-tree, to the deluder, to the mantra-deities of the jar and the sacred ford, to the essence of the Kalās, to the Ātma-tattva, Vidyā-tattva, and Śiva-tattva, to the one whose essence is complete—[I offer] the sandals.
(3) Having worshipped with the six limbs by means of the most formidable [mantra], |||
[Perform] the invocation and so forth; [offer] sandalwood, unbroken rice, and flowers with "Namaḥ. Display the *dhenumudrā*. [Recite] the *japa*.
oṃ juṃ saḥ svāhā (10) ||
Hymn of Praise.
Oṃ! One should worship the Lord with ten million offerings beginning with the goddesses, as well as with leaves, sprouts, the form of a pitcher,
cow’s milk, waters from sacred fords, a pond, fragrant fruits, medicinal herbs, jewels, divine parasols, parched grain and the like, honey, milk, vision, vermilion, and dūrvā grass.
I have no need for flowers, food offerings, incense, or full water-pots for the rites intended for those born of the dog lineage.
In this ritual for the worship of the hands, may all that be completely fulfilled.
[Then follows the ritual for the worship of the jar.]
The ritual placement (nyāsa).
Caṃ astrāya phaṭ || (4) || Cāṃ aṃguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ || Cīṃ tarjjanībhyāṃ [namaḥ] || (2) ||
Cūṃ, salutation to the two middle fingers; caiṃ, [salutation] to the two ring fingers; (2) cauṃ, salutation to the two little fingers; caḥ, salutation to the backs of both hands.
Cāṃ to the heart. (2) Cīṃ to the head, svāhā! Cūṃ to the tuft of hair, vaṣaṭ! Caiṃ to the armor, hūṃ!
*cauṃ* for the three eyes, *vauṣaṭ*; *caḥ* for the weapon (*astra*), *phaṭ*; [and] *ādhāraśaktaye*, etc.
Aiṃ (5), the sandals for the lion-throne.
Meditative absorption.
The Goddess is like the juice of lac, possessing a radiance equal to a ruby;
her limbs are variegated with all kinds of jewels, and Ambikā has assumed a physical form.
The goddess has eighteen arms and is intent on seizing various things;
bearing various jewels, such a goddess does not exist elsewhere in the three worlds.
The sword, the noose, the goad, the skull-cup, the thunderbolt, the banner,
the discus, the bell, and the ninth, which bestows boons.
In the upper hands, she holds a *pheṭaka*, a bow, a noose, a skull-topped staff (*khaṭvāṅga*), a water-pot (*kamaṇḍalu*),
a trident, a mallet, a lute, and a *gaṇārti*.
The river of the Mandaśaṃveṣṭha-vidyā, having spread forth as prosperity,
devours all the settlements arising from both the nectar and the non-nectar.
The flower of meditative concentration is the sandal.
Aiṁ (5) ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ, the sandal for the venerable Kulakumbha.
The worship of the three deities; the worship of Brahmāṇī and the others; the eight Aghoras beginning with Aśitāṅga.
Aiṃ (5) ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ! To Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda, the Lord of Heroes;
to the venerable Mahāvidyārājeśvarī HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ; to the venerable Kulakumbha, [I offer] the sandals. (3)
Aiṁ (5) Hsrūṁ Śrūṁ, the sandals for the venerable Kulakumbha.
Aiṃ (5) Śrūṃ Hsraṃ, the sandals for the venerable Kulakuṃbhabhartṛkā, the embodiment of the *alibali* offering.
Bali-vajra. The bali offering with the Aghora mantra: Hrāṃ to the heart (twice).

Hrīṁ to the head (2). Hrūṁ to the crest-lock (2). Hraiṁ to the armor (2). Hrauṁ to the eyes (2). Hraḥ to the weapon (2). Invocation and so forth; salutation to the sandalwood, unbroken rice grains, and flowers.
One should display the *yonimudrā*. [Offer] incense and a lamp. [Perform] the recitation (*jāpa*). *Śūṃ svāhā* (ten times).
Hymn of Praise.
Aiṁ. (5) Her body is like lac, vermilion, and the *bandhūka* flower, with a splendor resembling a ruby;

her face has three eyes and is adorned with golden ornaments. She holds a sword, a *pheṭaka*, and other implements in her hands, as well as the gestures of fearlessness (*abhaya*) and granting boons (*varada*). She bears the letter *Ka* and the *bindu*, and her golden limbs are radiant.
Homage to the divine cause, who resides upon a lion, possesses a universal form, and is bowed to by the three worlds.
In this ritual for the worship of the water-pot, may all that be completely fulfilled.
Then follows the purification of the Mahāpātra. [The ritual] placement (nyāsa): Hsauṃ, the pādukā for the thumb.
Hsauṃ, the *pādukā* for the index finger. Hsauṃ, the *pādukā* for the middle finger.
Hsauṃ, the sandals for the ring finger. Hsau, the sandals for the little finger.
Hsauṃ, the sandals for Karatarāya.
Hsauṃ, to the heart (2). Hsau, to the armor, svāhā! Hsauṃ, to the crest-lock, vaṣaṭ!
